text:
Carla S: FYI customer reported Dedicated dashboard showing 0 GPUs for their eu-west pool after they rotated a nodepool name earlier today.
Ben R: which cluster? any errors in the console?
Carla S: cluster: redwood-dedicated-eu1, nodepool renamed from np-gpu-old -> np-gpu-2026. Screenshot: https://files.redwood.internal/sup/shot123.png
Dmitri L: looking. Can you paste the panel query id? Also which inventory service version?
Carla S: panel id is metrics-panel-77, inventory service v2.3.4
Alice K: customer says API /v1/capacity/cluster returns empty nodes list too. They reported increased latency before it went blank.
Dmitri L: reproducing locally: after nodepool rename, our inventory-sync job filters by nodepool label "pool" and ignores nodes missing the old label. Seems the node relabel webhook updated k8s label but the inventory sync uses cached metadata keyed by nodepool name.
Carla S: oh no — rollout just replaced nodepool name, we didn't invalidate the cache.
Dmitri L: quick repro steps:
1) kubectl get nodes -l pool=np-gpu-2026
2) curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://console.redwood/api/v1/dedicated/capacity?cluster=redwood-dedicated-eu1
3) check inventory-sync logs: kubectl logs deploy/inventory-sync -n infra | grep "nodepool" 
I see entries: "skipping node X, nodepool key mismatch: expected np-gpu-old"
Ben R: any immediate mitigation for the customer?
Dmitri L: temporary workaround: trigger a full inventory resync: POST /internal/inventory/refresh?cluster=redwood-dedicated-eu1
Or restart inventory-sync deployment: kubectl rollout restart deploy/inventory-sync -n infra
I've run the refresh for this cluster just now (response 202). Waiting to see metrics backfill.
Support Bot: Created ticket TKT-4821 with priority P2, assigned to eng-sre. https://tickets.redwood.internal/TKT-4821
Alice K: customer on call wants ETA. Can we commit to a fix timeline?
Dmitri L: root cause: inventory keying by historical nodepool name means renames break matching. Fix approach: inventory-sync should prefer node UID and current labels, and invalidate pool-name index on rename. I'll open a PR with unit test, should be ready for review in ~3 business days. Hotfix: add a short-lived mapping patch to reconcile nodepool aliases — I can push it as a patch today and deploy to prod if approved.
Carla S: customer accepts the refresh workaround for now but asks for rollback-safe fix. They're concerned about repeated renames from autoscaling tooling.
Ben R: tagging eng-platform for potential API compatibility issues: @platform-team please review aliasing approach.
Dmitri L: action items:
- Dmitri: push hotfix patch and coordinate canary (today)
- Alice: update ticket TKT-4821 with workaround steps and notify customer (now)
- Platform: review aliasing design (ASAP)
Carla S: Sounds good. Will monitor dashboard; current watch: https://console.redwood/dedicated/redwood-dedicated-eu1/capacity
Ben R: metrics just started to come back for that cluster (observed at 1954323240). GPU counts incrementing.
Carla S: customer confirmed dashboard now shows GPUs again. Leaving ticket open until hotfix merged.
Dmitri L: I'll post PR link when ready and ping for review. Log snippet that indicated mismatch:
```
2026-09-12T14:05:21Z inventory-sync INFO skipping node ip-10-0-3-21: nodepool key mismatch expected=np-gpu-old actual=np-gpu-2026
```
Carla S: closing loop: customer reaction: "Thanks — dashboard looks normal now, appreciate the quick workaround." :thumbsup: 
Oncall SRE: assigning follow-up oncall rotation to validate similar rename patterns in other regions.
